treated_unit_rule: rows where the boolean column 'california' is True (verified to be state == 3 in all 31 years)

notes.outcome_meaning: cigsale = per-capita cigarette SALES in packs per person per year (tax-paid sales), not consumption. Source: data/README.md.
notes.treatment_variable: treated = (unit in treated_units) AND (time >= treatment_start). The file's 'after_treatment' column is a calendar-year dummy (year >= 1989) that is True for all 39 states and is NOT used as the treatment; see data/README.md, caveat 2.
notes.why_no_covariates: lnincome, beer and age15to24 are missing for all 39 states in many years (lnincome 1970-71 and 1998-2000; beer 1970-83 and 1998-2000; age15to24 1991-2000). Adding them would drop rows and change the estimand; plan.md test 1 says no covariates, and AGENTS.md forbids adding covariates without asking.
notes.treatment_timing: Single treated unit, single adoption date (1 January 1989). No staggered timing, so plain two-way fixed effects is not exposed to the Goodman-Bacon/negative-weighting problem.
notes.controls_choice: controls = [] means the other 38 states enter as pure two-way fixed effects (state and year dummies), i.e. all 1,209 rows are used.
notes.inference: cluster = state (39 clusters, but only 1 treated unit -> clustered SEs are unreliable; inference relies on the placebo test, as plan.md test 3 requires).
notes.after_treatment_column_check: script 01 checks that 'after_treatment' is True in 468 = 39*12 rows, i.e. 456 of them non-California, which is why it cannot be used as the treatment.
